headline: PENTAGON $400M BET DELIVERS: MP MATERIALS SHIPS GM'S FIRST NON-CHINESE RARE EARTH MAGNETS FROM FORT WORTH IN Q4 2026
snippet: MP Materials is on track for commercial rare earth magnet deliveries to General Motors in Q4 2026 from its 250,000-sq-ft Independence facility in Fort Worth, Texas, with magnets made from concentrate mined at Mountain Pass — the only operating rare earth mine and processing facility in the Americas. The Pentagon backed this milestone with a $400 million convertible preferred equity investment, a $150 million loan, and a 10-year offtake commitment at $110/kg NdPr, as China controls an estimated 60–70% of global mining and roughly 90% of processing capacity.

headline: COPPER MINERS SURGE 4-6% AS LME HITS $14,286/TONNE — FED HIKE ODDS COLLAPSE FROM 64% TO 18% ON 29,000-JOB PAYROLLS MISS
snippet: LME three-month copper rose to $14,286 a tonne Monday after September U.S. nonfarm payrolls came in at just 29,000 — the biggest miss in months — cutting the odds of an October Fed rate hike from 64% to 18% and sending copper miners sharply higher: Teck and Anglo American each gained as much as 6.1%, Glencore 4.6%, Freeport-McMoRan 4.1%, and Southern Copper 3.7%. The LME cash/three-month spread also flipped into backwardation for the first time in 2026, signalling near-term physical scarcity.

headline: MAIDEN DRILL CONFIRMS NEW COPPER DISCOVERY ACROSS 1.6KM STRIKE — JUST 9% OF 17KM TALISKER ANOMALY TESTED IN NUNAVUT
snippet: Somerset Minerals (ASX: SMM) confirmed a new copper-silver discovery at its Talisker target within the Coppermine Project in Nunavut, with maiden RC drilling returning TARC0003 at 36.58 metres grading 1.62% copper and 11.8 g/t silver (including 9.14 m at 4.39% Cu) and TARC0008 at 38.1 metres at 1.27% Cu. With ore-grade mineralisation now confirmed across 1.6 km of strike and assay results still pending for two of 14 holes, the company has tested only 9% of the full 17-kilometre Talisker anomaly.

headline: BUEN RETIRO HITS 30.5M AT 2.48% CU FROM SURFACE — FITZROY ADVANCING CHILE HEAP-LEACH AFTER 22,000M OF 2026 DRILLING
snippet: Fitzroy Minerals reported that drill hole BRT-DDH110 at the advanced Buen Retiro copper project in Chile intersected 30.5 metres grading 2.48% copper from surface to end-of-hole, with the hole ending prematurely in mineralization due to technical issues — leaving the system open at depth. With more than 22,000 metres of drilling completed in 2026 across multiple rigs, and environmental studies and engineering work advancing toward a potential heap-leach copper operation, Buen Retiro is building a near-term development case in a tier-1 Chilean copper district.

headline: GEIGER HITS AGAIN AT APOLLO — 45M OF NEAR-SURFACE URANIUM STARTING AT 40M DEPTH, SECOND KIGGAVIK-TREND DISCOVERY EXTENDS
snippet: Geiger Energy's second drill hole at the Apollo target in Nunavut (APL26-002) intersected 45 metres of elevated radioactivity starting at approximately 40 metres depth — shallower than the discovery hole — confirming the system extends 100 metres along strike on the Andrew Lake Fault that also hosts Orano's Kiggavik deposits. Apollo and the Fox discovery 10 km away were both generated from Geiger's geophysical interpretation in 2026 and were previously undrilled, establishing a new uranium district along one of Nunavut's most prospective structural corridors.

headline: LOCKHEED $58B PAC-3 + RTX $20.7B AMRAAM CONTRACTS PUT CRITICAL MINERAL SUPPLY CHAINS ON HIGH ALERT
snippet: Two landmark U.S. munitions contracts — Lockheed Martin's $58.62 billion PAC-3 MSE multiyear deal and RTX/Raytheon's $20.7 billion AMRAAM contract — are placing unprecedented strain on critical mineral supply chains including antimony (91% U.S. import-reliant), tungsten, and gallium that underpin modern precision munitions. The analysis cites the Pentagon's $450 million investment in The Elmet Group for domestic tungsten supply and the approaching November 27 China antimony export-control deadline as compounding the near-term availability risk.

headline: CAMBRIA GOLD GETS FINAL RED MOUNTAIN ROAD PERMIT — PREMIER GOLD 2,500 TPD MILL TARGETING Q4 2027 WITH C$45.9M RAISED
snippet: Cambria Gold Mines (TSX: CAMB) received the final Fisheries Act Authorization for the Red Mountain access road on September 21, allowing in-stream construction to proceed through Bitter Creek, and is targeting commissioning of the 2,500 tonne-per-day mill at the Premier Gold Project in Q4 2027 with ramp-up through 2028. The company has raised over C$45.9 million through warrant exercises to-date, and has expanded its engineering team with four senior professionals to de-risk critical permitting, infill drilling, and construction milestones ahead of production.

headline: BRAZIL SHUTS SIGMA LITHIUM'S GROTA DO CIRILO — SGML DROPS 13.4% AS REGULATOR CITES GEOTECHNICAL RISK, GUIDANCE CUT 30%
snippet: Brazil's National Mining Agency ordered Sigma Lithium (Nasdaq: SGML) to halt operations at part of its Grota do Cirilo complex in Minas Gerais on October 2, citing geotechnical risks on the eastern slope of the north pit — compounded by a federal court order from a quilombola communities lawsuit — sending shares down 13.4%. Sigma has cut its FY2027 lithium oxide concentrate production guidance from 330,000 tonnes to 240,000 tonnes while it awaits a federal appeals court ruling, with restart timing now uncertain.

headline: ZACATECAS SILVER GRABS OPTION ON GUANAJUATO EPITHERMAL — EL TIGRE VEIN 770M STRIKE FOR JUST $825K CASH AND SHARES
snippet: Zacatecas Silver signed a two-year option to acquire 100% of the Lourdes gold-silver project in Guanajuato, Mexico from Guanajuato Silver for US$225,000 in cash plus US$600,000 in shares — a low-cost entry into a low-sulphidation epithermal system with at least six mapped vein structures across 509 hectares, including the principal El Tigre vein traced over 770 metres of surface strike. A 2% NSR royalty applies on exercise, with half buyable for US$1 million, giving the acquirer a clear path to a clean royalty structure.

headline: GOLD CLINGS TO $4,138 SUPPORT AS OCTOBER FOMC LOOMS — ONE FED DECISION SEPARATES $4,400 BREAKOUT FROM $4,200 RETEST
snippet: Gold is holding the $4,100–$4,138 technical support zone after a pullback from its January record above $5,500, with the October 27–28 Fed meeting now set up as the binary macro catalyst: a pause would likely propel prices toward $4,400, while a rate hike could pressure the $4,200 level and test whether central bank structural buying (89% of reserve managers expect official gold holdings to rise over the next 12 months) holds the floor. The September payrolls miss has shifted odds sharply in gold's favour, but the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.22% remains the principal headwind.

headline: PENTAGON DROPS $450M ON TUNGSTEN VIA THE ELMET GROUP — U.S. MILITARY NEEDS 2,000-3,000 TONNES/YEAR WITH NEAR-ZERO DOMESTIC SUPPLY
snippet: The U.S. Department of Defense announced a $450 million investment in The Elmet Group to strengthen the domestic tungsten supply chain — a critical mineral used in bullets, missiles, and penetrators where the U.S. military consumes an estimated 2,000–3,000 metric tons annually and currently relies almost entirely on imports. The investment is part of a broader DoD critical minerals push following China's progressive export controls on tungsten, gallium, and antimony that began in 2023, and follows the MP Materials rare earth magnet bet announced last year.
